tagline: Up the west shore of Moosehead, then into the woods.
intro: Route 15 leaves Greenville beside Moosehead Lake and runs up to Rockwood, on the west side of the lake, then on through the woods to Jackman.

Moosehead is the largest lake in Maine, about 40 miles by 10, and takes its name from the way it looks on a map, like an antlered moose. The highway came late to it. Route 15 reached Rockwood around 1934 and Jackman only in 1940.

moments.title: Greenville
moments.text: Henry Gower cleared land by the lake here in 1835 and put up the first hotel, a two-story building he called the Seboomook House.

moments.title: Mount Kineo
moments.text: Across the water from Rockwood its cliffs rise 700 feet straight out of the lake, and the state park around them can only be reached by boat.

moments.title: Jackman
moments.text: The road ends at US 201 in a town named for Captain James Jackman, whom the state hired in the 1830s to build the road through to Canada.
